documents.unit: Office of the Provost / AI Working Group
documents.title: Michigan Tech Syllabus Guidance
documents.summary: Provides three instructor-adoptable syllabus templates (general permission, conditional permission, prohibition) plus an example HU 3015 statement. All carry disclosure and student-responsibility language.
documents.stance_why: The page offers "three tiers—General Permission, Conditional Permission, and Prohibition" that instructors adapt, so the document sets no stance of its own and hands the choice to instructors; tiers listed.

units.why: The page frames its three templates as named tiers; "categorized into three tiers" is a statement that uses of GAI are sorted into levels, so P05 (named tiers) fits better than P04 because the tiers are explicit.
units.anchor: categorized into three tiers—General Permission, Conditional Permission, and Prohibition

units.why: The working group offers templates "to guide instructors in establishing" GAI policies "within their courses" and says they are "adaptable", so the decision is left to each instructor; this is P04 rather than P05 because the point is who decides.
units.anchor: to guide instructors in establishing generative artificial intelligence (GAI) use policies within their courses
units.frag_start: The AI Working Group at Michigan

units.why: The group "encourages" pairing templates with "class discussions or lessons on AI literacy", a recommendation that courses teach about AI, so P44 (teach effective AI use as a skill) is the nearest type.
units.anchor: templates to be paired with class discussions or lessons on AI literacy
units.frag_end: facilitating those conversations can be found

units.why: Instructors are "advised to regularly consult" the integrity policy, research integrity policies and the Provost AI page "to stay informed"; this is advice that faculty keep up with AI policy, i.e. P63 (support faculty in learning AI).
units.anchor: Instructors are advised to regularly consult the MTU Academic Integrity Policy
units.frag_end: the latest AI tools and policy updates

units.why: General Permission template: the instructor "expects that students will incorporate these technologies into their classwork", which makes AI use the expected default and is P02.
units.anchor: the instructor expects that students will incorporate these technologies into their classwork as appropriate
units.frag_end: of their abilities to engage with these new tools

units.why: The template cites "the increasing integration of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools" in professions and says work will be treated "as a demonstration of their abilities to engage with these new tools"; this is a career rationale, P44.
units.anchor: treat the work students produce as a demonstration of their abilities

units.why: "The use of GAI tools is permitted" is the template's default allowance, so P02; the condition about critical thinking is coded separately.
units.anchor: The use of GAI tools is permitted
units.frag_start: The use of GAI tools is

units.why: Use "should be accompanied by critical thinking and reflection" asks students to evaluate and reflect on AI use; P31 (verify and critically evaluate) fits better than P32 because it concerns evaluating output and not who solves the problem.
units.anchor: their use should be accompanied by critical thinking and reflection
units.frag_start: The use of GAI tools is

units.why: "Responsibility for the work's integrity remains with the student, including any inaccuracies stemming from AI use" makes students answerable for submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: Responsibility for the work's integrity remains with the student

units.why: "Transparency in AI tool usage is mandatory" is a requirement to disclose AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Transparency in AI tool usage is mandatory

units.why: "instructors reserve the right to ask students to explain their process for creating work at any time" is a check of understanding by explanation, P34.
units.anchor: reserve the right to ask students to explain their process for creating work

units.why: "including prompt appendices, AI-generated outputs, and reflective analyses" lists the documentation students include; P26 (keep and submit transcripts, outputs, reflections) fits better than P25 because it names appendices and reflections rather than citation details.
units.anchor: including prompt appendices, AI-generated outputs, and reflective analyses

units.why: "Students in this course are expected to use [citation style]" with guidance on citing AI in that style sets an expectation to cite AI, P24.
units.anchor: Students in this course are expected to use [citation style]
units.frag_end: within this style can be found at

units.why: For courses that submit work to journals or funders, "being aware of their policies is important before beginning work"; this defers to venue and funder rules on GAI, which is P62.
units.anchor: being aware of their policies is important before beginning work
units.frag_end: on the use of GAI can be found

units.why: "Course policies therefore are provisional and subject to change" says the policy will change as tools do, P54.
units.anchor: Course policies therefore are provisional and subject to change

units.why: "Students should consult the instructor if they have any questions about the permissible use of technology" tells unsure students to ask first, P10.
units.anchor: Students should consult the instructor if they have any questions about the permissible use

units.why: Conditional Permission template: GAI "may be permitted or recommended for specific assignments", so permission is set per assignment, P04 and not P02 because AI is not allowed by default.
units.anchor: may be permitted or recommended for specific assignments in this course

units.why: "Those assignments that allow or call for GAI use will be expressly listed as such" requires the instructor to state AI expectations in assignment instructions, P09.
units.anchor: will be expressly listed as such

units.why: Assignments that allow AI "require proper citation and documentation according to [citation style]", a citation requirement, P24.
units.anchor: require proper citation and documentation according to [citation style]

units.why: "The use of AI for assistance in completing other coursework is prohibited" bans AI wherever it is not expressly allowed, which is P01; the cheating label is coded separately as P36.
units.anchor: The use of AI for assistance in completing other coursework is prohibited

units.why: AI use outside permitted assignments "constitutes cheating", so it is classed as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: constitutes cheating

units.anchor: is strictly prohibited in all coursework

units.why: The ban names "ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Dall-e, etc." to say which tools and apps the policy covers, which defines scope, P61.
units.anchor: tools and apps (e.g. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Dall-e, etc.)
units.frag_start: The use of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools and apps

units.why: Use "will be considered the use of an unauthorized aide, which is a form of cheating" classifies it as misconduct, P36.

units.why: HU 3015 example: students "are permitted to use AI tools such as ChatGPT for assistance with homework, labs, reports, and study materials", a broad allowance, P02.
units.anchor: permitted to use AI tools such as ChatGPT for assistance with homework, labs, reports

units.why: "any significant assistance received from such tools be properly attributed in the submitted work" is an attribution requirement, P24.
units.anchor: any significant assistance received from such tools be properly attributed

units.why: The sample statement "I utilized [AI Tool Name] to assist with [specific aspect" shows an attribution naming the tool and the use; P25 (tool and details in the citation) fits better than P24 because it prescribes content.
units.anchor: I utilized [AI Tool Name] to assist with [specific aspect, e.g., generating ideas

units.why: "You should refrain from using artificial intelligence (AI) to generate text or responses to graded assignments unless permitted" bans AI-produced submissions, P19.
units.anchor: refrain from using artificial intelligence (AI) to generate text or responses

units.why: "Open AI's Chat GPT 4 was utilized to assist in revising this document" is the issuing group disclosing its own AI use; P47 (disclose instructor/staff AI use) is the nearest type.
units.anchor: Chat GPT 4 was utilized to assist in revising this document

documents.title: 1.20 Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools
documents.summary: Official policy 1.20 sets five considerations (data submission, consent, review, compliance, disclosure) for anyone at the university using generative AI. It focuses on data protection and output checking and does not address classroom rules.
documents.stance_why: It allows AI use by affiliates with conditions: "Avoid submitting MTU data classified as tier 1", "Review the output", and disclosure when use is "more than 25%" of a deliverable; nothing bans AI.

units.why: The introduction says AI "can be used to significant positive benefit but can also be misused", a framing statement for the policy, P56.
units.anchor: can be used to significant positive benefit but can also be misused

units.why: "To ensure responsible use ... this policy provides high level considerations and guidance" states the purpose and scope of an institution-wide framework, P56.
units.anchor: this policy provides high level considerations and guidance for University affiliates
units.frag_start: To ensure responsible use of tools

units.why: "Administrative units of MTU may devise their own AI-related policies and procedures consistent with this policy" lets units set their own rules, P04.
units.anchor: may devise their own AI-related policies and procedures consistent with this policy

units.why: "Avoid submitting MTU data classified as tier 1" tells affiliates not to put confidential data into AI tools, P50.
units.anchor: Avoid submitting MTU data classified as tier 1

units.why: "only publicly available or non-sensitive data should be shared with AI tools" limits what data may be given to AI, P50.
units.anchor: only publicly available or non-sensitive data should be shared with AI tools

units.why: "Generally, there is no expectation of privacy when using AI tools" is a statement that AI tools may store or reuse prompts, P50.
units.anchor: there is no expectation of privacy when using AI tools
units.frag_end: subsequent request by an unaffiliated entity.

units.why: Tier 1 data may be used with an AI tool "only with the written consent of the Chief Information Officer, Chief Information Security Officer, or General Counsel" where a contract protects data; an exception procedure, P50.
units.anchor: only with the written consent of the Chief Information Officer
units.frag_start: Where a contract or other legal agreement

units.why: "Obtain the consent of data owners before sharing any data with AI tools" is a data-consent requirement, P50.
units.anchor: Obtain the consent of data owners before sharing any data with AI tools
units.frag_start: Obtain the consent of data owners

units.why: "Inform participants if AI tools will be used in meetings or other shared engagements" requires telling others about AI use; no type is exact, P47 (disclosure of AI use to those affected) is closest.
units.anchor: Inform participants if AI tools will be used in meetings or other shared engagements
units.frag_start: Obtain the consent of data owners

units.why: "Participants must have the ability to opt-out of such use" gives people a way out of AI use, P51 (optional, alternatives).
units.anchor: Participants must have the ability to opt-out of such use

units.why: "If the data owner cannot be identified, the data cannot be used with any AI tools" is a flat limit on data use, P50.
units.anchor: If the data owner cannot be identified, the data cannot be used

units.why: "even publicly available data may be protected by copyright" warns about copyright in inputs, P52.
units.anchor: even publicly available data may be protected by copyright
units.frag_start: Note that even publicly available data

units.why: "Review the output of AI tools prior to use or publication to ensure accuracy and relevance" requires checking AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Review the output of AI tools prior to use or publication
units.frag_start: Review the output of AI tools

units.why: "AI tools may exhibit bias based on the data used for training" names bias as a concern, P53.
units.anchor: AI tools may exhibit bias based on the data used for training
units.frag_start: Research has shown that AI tools

units.why: Affiliates "must evaluate the output of any AI tool" so it "does not infringe on copyright or violate any laws or ethical norms"; the copyright and law element makes P52 the better home than P31, which is coded in the Review item.
units.anchor: does not infringe on copyright or violate any laws or ethical norms
units.frag_start: MTU affiliates must evaluate the output

units.why: "Ensure compliance with applicable laws, university policies, and relevant terms of use or license agreements" covers terms of use of AI tools, P52.
units.anchor: Ensure compliance with applicable laws, university policies, and relevant terms of use or license agreements
units.frag_end: data being supplied to the tools.

units.why: "Disclose use of AI tools as required by the entity receiving the AI-facilitated content" requires disclosure of AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Disclose use of AI tools as required by the entity receiving

units.why: Disclosure is required "in all cases" where AI is a significant component, defined as "more than 25% of the final product/deliverable", a numeric disclosure threshold, P24.
units.anchor: this means more than 25% of the final product/deliverable

units.why: "MTU affiliates are encouraged to disclose any use of AI tools" extends disclosure to all use as a recommendation, P24.
units.anchor: MTU affiliates are encouraged to disclose any use of AI tools

units.why: "Failure to disclose the use of AI tools ... could lead to allegations of plagiarism or academic or professional misconduct" makes non-disclosure the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Failure to disclose the use of AI tools in the development of any deliverable

units.why: "Academic integrity and professional ethics require honesty and transparency" states the principle behind disclosure, P56.
units.anchor: Academic integrity and professional ethics require honesty and transparency

units.why: The definition says generative AI refers to "tools that have been trained with datasets and which can create new and original content", which sets what the policy covers, P61.
units.anchor: generative artificial intelligence refers to artificial intelligence tools that have been trained with datasets
units.frag_end: when prompted by the user of the tool.
